notes.1: This question was answered very well. Most candidates accurately differentiated twice to find the Maclaurin’s series, though a few worked with an erroneous value of f’(0) without checking their work.
notes.2: A few candidates spent time finding det ( A−λI ) instead of reading directly from the diagonal of the matrix. Better responses maintained accuracy throughout the solution, both when manipulating the characteristic equation and when substituting A and A3.
notes.3a: The first part of this question was answered well by most candidates.
notes.3b: Candidates who used the chain rule were usually successful. It was not uncommon for those who chose to multiply out the expression to introduce errors during this process. A small number of candidates made y' the subject before differentiating using the quotient rule and were usually successful also.
notes.4a: The more successful approaches formed a correct expression for the sum of the areas of the rectangles and integrated by parts to accurately derive the given result.
notes.4b: Some candidates recognised that they could adapt their solution to part (a) and by accurately doing so generally went on to derive a suitable lower bound.
notes.5: Almost all knew how to approach this question and completed it to a high standard. There was some inaccuracy when solving linear equations to find the particular integral and some errors when substituting initial conditions. A few candidates gave expressions instead of equations as their answer.
notes.6a: Most candidates used de Moivre’s theorem successfully to find cosec5θ. Some candidates has difficulty translating their expression in cos and sin into an expression in cosec. There were some elegant uses of cot2θ=cosec2θ−1 and good candidates showed full details of their working.
notes.6b: Some candidates made the connection with the equation given in the first part and, justifying the relationship, used that cosec5θ=2 to find all five solutions in an efficient manner.
notes.7a: This was done well with the majority of candidates dividing through by x2−1 and then arriving at the given integrating factor using the logarithmic form cosh−1x.
notes.7b: Better responses maintained accuracy throughout, with candidates fully simplifying the right hand side of the equation after multiplying by the integrating factor. The integral of the right hand side could then clearly be seen as x2−1+C and the initial conditions substituted to find the correct value of C.
notes.8a: This part of the question was well done with the majority of candidates accurately substituting cosh in terms of exponentials and writing out the full expansion of cosh2A to justify the given identity.
notes.8b: (i) Most candidates accurately recalled the formula for surface area, applying cosh2A=sinh2A+1 after expanding to reach the given answer.
notes.8bii: After multiplying out ( 2cosh2t+3t ) cosh2t, the best responses maintained accuracy by applying integration by parts and the necessary hyperbolic identities. Appling integration by parts before or after expanding were the two different approaches seen, with the latter approach being more efficient since tcosh2t gives an odd function. A few candidates gave an answer involving sinh or cosh instead of converting their answer to one in terms of π and e.
notes.key_messages:
• Candidates should show all the steps in their solutions, particularly when proving a given result.
• Candidates should read questions carefully so that they answer all aspects in adequate depth,
particularly when approximating the area under a curve using rectangles.
• Candidates should make use of results derived or given in earlier parts of a question.
notes.general_comments:
The majority of candidates demonstrated very good knowledge across the whole syllabus and there were
many scripts of a high standard. They showed their working clearly and were accurate in their handling of
algebra and calculus. They also showed a good understanding of linear algebra. Sometimes candidates did
not fully justify their answers and reached conclusions without supporting justification, particularly where
answers were given within the question.
